headline: Elevated, steady: oil barely moved when markets reopened after Iran's unconfirmed supertanker-sinking claim, and Coles is investigating a cyber attack but says shop as normal.
summary: Brent oil opened the week slightly lower at about US$95.50, so Iran's still-unconfirmed claim that a supertanker sank in Hormuz has not yet pushed prices up; Hormuz traffic stays at about 4 ships a day and Australia remains at Level 2 of the National Fuel Security Plan. Coles is investigating a cyber security incident, says there is no evidence customer data was taken and that stores are trading normally. Overnight GPS-jamming flags over Israel, the Gulf and the Black Sea were not linked to any new attack, and Microsoft 365 is restored with a cyber attack ruled out. Locally it is quiet: Moderate fire danger in the Hills, no fire bans or CFS warnings, and the grid and phone networks are normal.
actions: Be wary of emails or texts claiming to be from Coles about the cyber incident; go to the Coles app or website directly rather than clicking links.
Keep the car topped up as normal; no fuel price jump yet, but Gulf claims are still unresolved.

categories.name: Geopolitical & conflict
categories.summary: Iran's claim that a supertanker with about 2 million barrels sank after a mine blast is still not independently confirmed; reports mention an Iranian drone attack on Bahrain but this run could not confirm a new one. Gulf GPS jamming has eased to 17% and Israel to 0%; Black Sea data is missing. Taiwan, Korea and Russia-NATO show no new warning signs.

sources.title: Malay Mail: Iran says supertanker sank in Hormuz after hitting mine

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal, no unusual private-jet movements, and forecast markets show no jump.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure
categories.summary: Coles is investigating a cyber security incident; it says there is no evidence customer data was taken and customers can shop as normal. Microsoft 365 is fully restored and Microsoft has ruled out a cyber attack. All Australian carriers and the SA grid are normal; the global threat level is green.

sources.title: Canberra Times: 'Shop as normal': Coles investigates cyber attack

categories.name: Pandemic & biological
categories.summary: WHO reports the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continuing in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria and MERS in Qatar and Saudi Arabia, with no spread beyond those regions. A WHO note on pneumonia of unknown cause in Russia and an earlier Burundi illness cluster show no sign of wider spread. No Adelaide emergency departments are very busy.

sources.title: WHO: Ebola (Bundibugyo) - DRC, Kenya and Nigeria

categories.name: Natural hazards
categories.summary: Fire danger Moderate in the Mount Lofty Ranges today and tomorrow, no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans or CFS warnings. A severe thunderstorm warning covers the far North West Pastoral district only, and outback roads in the north-east remain closed by flooding.

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply
categories.summary: Hormuz carries about 4 ships a day (100+ before the war). Australia remains at Level 2 of the National Fuel Security Plan. Malacca, Lombok, Sunda and Torres routes are normal, and Coles stores are trading despite the cyber incident.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: Markets shrugged off the weekend Hormuz claims: Brent about US$95.50 (down 0.4%), VIX 19.3, gold US$3,870. The ASX dipped on miners and the Australian dollar eased to about 67.6 US cents.

concerns.title: Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz shipping
drivers: Iran says a supertanker carrying about 2 million barrels sank in Hormuz after a mine blast; this is still not independently confirmed.
Oil barely moved when markets reopened (Brent about US$95.50), Hormuz carries about 4 ships a day, and Gulf GPS jamming has eased to 17%.
Forecast markets give about 16% for a US-Iran Hormuz deal by year end.

scenarios.name: Standoff drags on with mine and ship incidents
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices stay high; occasional regional servo shortages but no rationing.

scenarios.name: Deal reached, shipping recovers
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices ease over weeks; little direct effect on SA.

scenarios.name: Major escalation: renewed US/Israeli strike campaign or wider Gulf attacks
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel price jump and local shortages within 1-3 weeks; possible government fuel measures.

actions.action: Keep the car at least half full.
actions.reason: A sudden escalation would push bowser prices up within days, and queues form fast.

actions.action: Hold a little cash at home.
actions.reason: If fuel is rationed or networks fail, cash still works when cards may not.

concerns.title: Cyber attacks and outages hitting Australian services
drivers: Coles is investigating a cyber security incident; it says there is no evidence customer data was taken and stores are trading normally.
Microsoft 365 is restored and was not an attack; Australian carriers and the SA grid are normal and the global threat level is green.

scenarios.name: Ongoing breaches and occasional cloud outages
scenarios.sa_impact: Hours of disruption to some online services; scam risk from stolen data.

scenarios.name: Hours-long outage of payments, a retailer or a telco
scenarios.sa_impact: Card payments, online orders or phones down for hours.

scenarios.name: Multi-day multi-sector attack
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, fuel and communications disrupted for days.

actions.action: Treat any 'Coles' email or text about the incident with suspicion.
actions.reason: Scammers follow news of breaches with fake notices; go to the official app or site directly.

concerns.title: AI-enabled attack (non-traditional)
drivers: The FBI has warned an open-source AI security tool is being used in cyber attacks worldwide, and a French bank reportedly lost about EUR 100 million in an attack likely aided by AI; none target Australia specifically.
No deepfakes of officials or fake alerts have been reported in Australia.

scenarios.name: Background AI-assisted crime and espionage
scenarios.sa_impact: More convincing scams and data breaches; no wide outage.

scenarios.name: Synthetic-media crisis (fake leader video or alert)
scenarios.sa_impact: Hours of confusion, possible panic buying before it is debunked.

scenarios.name: Machine-speed attack on many systems at once
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, telcos, hospitals or the grid disrupted for hours to days.

actions.action: Agree a family code word for urgent calls.
actions.reason: AI can clone a voice from seconds of audio; a code word defeats fake 'I need help now' calls.

concerns.title: Local SA emergency (bushfire, heat, power) within 7 days
drivers: Fire danger is Moderate in the Hills and there is no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans or CFS warnings.
A severe thunderstorm warning covers only the far North West Pastoral district; the SA grid is normal and the low midday demand is rooftop solar, not an outage.

scenarios.name: Quiet week
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Hot, windy day with fire bans
scenarios.sa_impact: Fire danger High to Extreme in the Hills; travel plans may need changing.

scenarios.name: Damaging fire or major power outage
scenarios.sa_impact: Evacuations, power and phone outages in affected areas.

actions.action: Check your bushfire plan and the CFS app alert zones before the first hot spell.
actions.reason: Early-season fires start fast, and decisions are easier made on a calm day.

concerns.title: Taiwan Strait pressure
drivers: No live-fire warnings, GPS jamming or internet disruption around Taiwan; strait shipping is normal.
Forecast markets give about 3% for a China-Taiwan clash before 2027; Quad leaders meeting is diplomatic signalling, not escalation.

scenarios.name: Routine grey-zone pressure
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Large announced drill
scenarios.sa_impact: Market jitters; no supply effect.

scenarios.name: Blockade or quarantine
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel, medicine and electronics disruption within weeks.

actions.action: Keep 2-3 months of any essential prescription medicines.
actions.reason: Most medicines are imported via Asian shipping lanes, which any blockade would disrupt first.

concerns.title: Ebola in Africa and MERS in the Gulf
drivers: WHO reports the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continuing in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria with no cases outside Africa, and MERS cases in Qatar and Saudi Arabia linked to camel contact.
No Adelaide emergency departments are very busy.

scenarios.name: Outbreaks stay contained in their regions
scenarios.sa_impact: No direct effect; possible extra airport screening.

scenarios.name: Isolated imported case in a Western country
scenarios.sa_impact: Media concern; Australian hospitals manage under existing plans.

scenarios.name: Spread in Asia-Pacific
scenarios.sa_impact: Travel restrictions and health system alerts.

actions.action: Check Smartraveller before any travel to Central or East Africa or the Gulf.
actions.reason: Advice and entry rules can change quickly as outbreaks and the conflict develop.

concerns.title: Undersea cables and Australian networks
drivers: No foreign vessels are on the cable watch list near Australia and all Australian carriers are normal.
No undersea cable damage reported near Australia.

scenarios.name: Routine shipping, no damage
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Single cable damaged
scenarios.sa_impact: Slower international internet for days; traffic reroutes via other cables.

scenarios.name: Several cables cut at once
scenarios.sa_impact: Major internet, payments and cloud disruption across Australia.

actions.reason: EFTPOS and card payments are the first thing to fail in a network outage.
